subject: Next steps: DPA routing, SCC module options & security questionnaire
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Taylor <sophie.taylor@finlypay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & asks — DPA, SCC module, and SQ kickoff

Hi Sophie — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can align on contracting path and security evidence.

Call highlights (short):
- Finly is evaluating Redwood for payments fraud detection and routing.
- You confirmed preference for data residency in the EU and need to understand controller/processor roles for the integration.
- SOC 2 status: you asked whether Redwood has a current SOC 2 report and what parts of our environment it covers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Finly will be the data controller for this integration (my assumption from the call: yes).
2) Review the attached security questionnaire (you mentioned a short SQ) and send it back — I’ve attached our DPA draft as a starting point.
3) SCC module: we typically propose Module 2 (controller-to-processor) for EU-only flows but are happy to propose Module 3 where required; if you have a legal preference, flag it.
4) I’ll loop in Legal (Laura) to draft a DPA with the correct SCC insert and circulate a DocuSign link for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_20260925.pdf; Redwood_SOC2-Summary-2026Q2.pdf

Can you confirm the controller stance and who on your side will own the legal/security review? If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call next week.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sophie Taylor <sophie.taylor@finlypay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael O'Connor <m.oconnor@finlypay.com>, security@finlypay.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:34:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & asks — DPA, SCC module, and SQ kickoff

Thanks Neha — great call. Confirming: Finly will be the controller of the transaction and we expect vendors to act as processors for transaction-level data.

On SCC module: our legal team prefers the controller-to-processor pathway (Module 2) for EU customer data. If Redwood believes Module 3 is more appropriate because of cross-border subprocessors, please call that out in the DPA language.

I've attached our security questionnaire (Finly_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — it is short but includes SOC 2 scope & encryption questions. Michael will coordinate the legal review.

Sophie
Sophie Taylor
Head of Security & Privacy, Finly Payments
sophie.taylor@finlypay.com

Hi Sophie — thanks for confirming. Next actions on our side:
- Laura (Legal) will update the DPA to reflect controller-to-processor (Module 2) language and call out the subprocessors list and cross-border subprocessors; David (Security) will map the SOC 2 coverage to the items in your SQ and send a short evidence packet.
- I’ll share a DocuSign link to the DPA once Laura finalizes the insert.

Tentative timeline:
- Laura will circulate a redline by Tue EOD (28 Sep).
- David will upload a SOC 2 summary and relevant attestations by Wed (29 Sep).
- After Finly legal confirms, we’ll aim for DocuSign signature the same week.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_20260925.pdf (updated to include Module 2 notes)

If you prefer a dedicated legal-to-legal call, we’re available Wed 29 Sep 10:00–11:00 CET or Thu 30 Sep 09:00–10:00 CET.

Best — Neha

Thanks all — quick note from Finly Legal: we reviewed the draft and Module 2 looks right. A couple of asks before signing:
- Please add a 30-day deletion SLA for sandbox/test data and a clear subprocessors notification window (we typically request 15 days).
- Can Redwood confirm encryption-at-rest coverage for KV cache and backups (we saw a line in the SOC 2 summary but need specifics)?

We’ll aim to return redlines by Thu EOD. Sophie/security will follow up on the SQ.

On scheduling: Wed 29 Sep 10:00 CET didn't work for us; Thu 30 Sep 09:00 CET is good — we'll put calendar invites.

Regards,
Michael O'Connor
